_readme: Our set slug -> the same set's id on TCGdex, for the English card checklists.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. api.pokemontcg.io gave us card COUNTS but we never had
a card LIST, so the 23 English guides showed rarity totals and 8 chase cards
and nothing else, while the 13 imported guides listed every card. TCGdex has
all 218 English sets with per-card rarity, images, and TCGplayer market
prices in USD refreshed daily, which is more than we had from either source.
EVERY ENTRY WAS VERIFIED, not guessed: all 28 matched TCGdex on BOTH the set
name and the exact total card count, with no near-misses and no ambiguity.
sync-cards.mjs re-checks the count on every run and warns if one drifts, so a
renamed or re-scoped set upstream cannot silently swap a checklist.
The five Sword & Shield sets at the bottom were added on 2026-08-15 and were
checked the same way, against BOTH APIs independently, and the two agree on
every count: Crown Zenith 160, Celebrations 25, Chilling Reign 233, Shining
Fates 73, Rebel Clash 209. Each also has a near neighbour on TCGdex that is a
DIFFERENT set and must not be picked by mistake: swsh12.5gg (Crown Zenith
Galarian Gallery), cel25cc (Celebrations Classic Collection) and swsh4.5sv
(Shining Fates Shiny Vault) are subsets sold inside the same product.
Ids follow TCGdex's own scheme, which is not pokemontcg.io's: sv08.5 where
the other API said sv8pt5, me05 where it said me5, swsh4.5 where it said
swsh45. Do not derive one from the other, they disagree on padding and on
the .5 sets.
FOUR SETS WERE CONSIDERED ON 2026-08-21 AND ALL FOUR WERE REJECTED, and the
argument is written here so nobody has to price it a second time. Today's
import named Silver Tempest, Lost Origin and Scarlet & Violet Black Star
Promos for the first time, and four hit cards had nowhere to resolve: three
on cg0H0ipfB90 and one on XjFoToaom6k.
ADDING A SET IS NOT AN EDIT TO THIS FILE. The root gate is SET_MAP in
scripts/sync-sets.mjs, because sync-cards.mjs skips any slug that is 'not in
sets.json', and four more maps want the same line: TCG_SET in
shared/tcgplayer.mjs, SET_MAP in scripts/sync-wanted.mjs, CARD_SETS in
shared/taxonomy.mjs and PC_CONSOLES in shared/pricecharting.mjs. A slug that
gets through then generates a /sets/<id>.html guide with no gate at all, plus
a sitemap url, a tile on /sets/index.html, and rows on /complete-a-set.html,
/cards.html, /what-set.html, /luck.html and /expansions.html. For these two
that is 2 new pages, 2 sitemap urls, 432 new card records, and 279 EXISTING
/pokemon/ pages that already print those two set names and would gain
checklist-backed rows (counted from the built tree). The guides would also
ship with no logo and no notes: nothing has been drawn for either set and
data/set-notes.json has no entry, both of which degrade quietly rather than
failing, so the cost is a thin page rather than a broken one.
WHAT IT WOULD HAVE BOUGHT IS 2 CARDS OF THE 21, AND BOTH ON A GUESS.
Measured against TCGdex the same day, swsh12 is 215 of 215 cards with a scan
and swsh11 is 217 of 217, so Reshiram V and Galarian Perrserker V really do
resolve. But the log records no rarity for either, and Silver Tempest prints
Reshiram V TWICE (024 Holo Rare V, 172 Ultra Rare) while Lost Origin prints
Galarian Perrserker V THREE times (129, 183, 184). Both would land on
resolveHits' same[0] fallback in build-pages.mjs, so each page would state a
collector number and show a scan the rip log cannot support. The cheap fix is
a rarity in column K of the workbook, not two set guides.
AND THE OTHER TWO CARDS ARE IN NEITHER SET, which is the swsh12.5gg warning
above arriving a second time. Corviknight V Trainer Gallery is swsh12.5tg, a
30 card companion set, and Victini is svp-208. Counted from TCGdex on
2026-08-21: swsh12.5tg carries a scan for 0 of its 30 cards, swsh12.5gg for 0
of its 70, and svp for 192 of 226 with 208 among the 34 blanks. All three
assets answer 404. So no amount of set-adding gives those cards a picture
FROM THIS HOST, and a set is the wrong lever for them.
THE SCANS DO EXIST, ON TWO HOSTS imgDims() IN shared/format.mjs ALREADY
KNOWS, and that is the cheaper thing to do instead. Fetched and eyeballed the
same day, all 200: images.pokemontcg.io/swsh12tg/TG18.png is Corviknight V
TG18 (170,928 bytes, 245x342) and .../swsh12pt5gg/GG32.png is Paras GG32
(176,121 bytes), which is the Crown Zenith hit on U91JWMsUHAU; and
images.scrydex.com/pokemon/svp-208/small is Victini (50,772 bytes, 245x342).
THAT PRECEDENT SENTENCE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE RATHER THAN DELETED.
It read: a pokemontcg.io card scan is already hotlinked on
/sets/celebrations.html. It is not. No set guide on this site makes a single
request to pokemontcg.io or to scrydex. The one live hotlink is Celebrations
#25 Mew on a RIP page, and it is not hand-typed either: sync-sets.mjs writes
it into public/data/sets.json's chase list because TCGdex 404s that card, and
it is 1 of 224 chase images. So the site has never hand-typed a card image
url, and three would have been the first.
A follow-up pass costed the three anyway and DECLINED them, for reasons worth
keeping: nothing would notice one dying (sweep-scans.mjs is TCGdex-only, and
onerror=this.remove() makes a dead url silent, which is the exact failure
data/no-scan.json exists to prevent); two of the three keys are workbook
strings the build is actively telling Tim to fix, so a hand key on them gets
LESS correct after he fixes them; and all three cards already sit in
public/data/printings/*.json with the right set and number, lacking only an
image, so the fix belongs in sync-all-printings.mjs. build-cards.mjs already
argues the general form of that: a page builder rewriting a sync's output is
undone by the next sync.
The per-card urls above were all verified 200 and are kept as evidence. What
is recorded here is where the next person will come looking.
